How did a failed World War II experiment become one of the most useful adhesives ever invented?

In 1942, American chemist Harry Coover and his team at Eastman Kodak were searching for clear plastic materials for military gun sights.

Instead, they encountered an unusual chemical: cyanoacrylate.

There was one huge problem.

It stuck to almost everything.

Glass. Tools. Laboratory equipment.

Tendon training is the missing piece of strength: muscle doesn’t touch the bone, tendons do, and they set the ceiling on how much of your strength you can actually use. Here are 5 no-equipment tendon exercises you can do in under 5 minutes.

▶Feel ten years younger👉 https://greyguyfitness.com/

In this video:

Dead hang: stronger forearms, elbows and shoulders
Wall sit: slow, steady tension for the tendons around your knee
Eccentric heel drop: the Achilles tendon, explained with the research
Isometric push-up hold: the push side of your upper body
Glute bridge hold: the tendons behind your hip

outliers.title: 30 Genius 1980s Inventions That FAILED Miserably!
outliers.description:
These are 30 genius 1980s inventions that failed miserably, from a camera with pictures smaller than your thumbnail to a computer you fixed by dropping it.
Among the 80s gadgets, the Kodak Disc camera made grainy prints and the Coleco Adam drew its power from its own printer. Apple told Apple III owners to drop the computer, then buried about 2,700 Apple Lisa machines in a Utah landfill. Cars joined the list of 1980s inventions that failed, from the stainless steel DeLorean to the Cadillac Allanté, whose bodies flew in from Italy.

outliers.title: How One Failed Experiment Became Super Glue #shorts #documentary
outliers.description:
How did a failed World War II experiment become one of the most useful adhesives ever invented?

In 1942, American chemist Harry Coover and his team at Eastman Kodak were searching for clear plastic materials for military gun sights.

Instead, they encountered an unusual chemical: cyanoacrylate.

There was one huge problem.

It stuck to almost everything.

Glass. Tools. Laboratory equipment.

For the scientists, this was a failure. They needed a material that could be shaped into precision parts, not one that bonded uncontrollably to nearby surfaces.
